Tech Report: Unconventional resistivity reduction in NbP semimetal nanoribbons

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 26 min read (5210 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~26 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Modern and future electronics harbour a key challenge: as conventional metal wires shrink to nanoscale dimensions, their resistivity increases sharply1 owing to surface and grain-boundary scattering.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Modern and future electronics harbour a key challenge: as conventional metal wires shrink to nanoscale dimensions, their resistivity increases sharply1 owing to surface and grain-boundary scattering. To circumvent this unwanted behaviour, here, we explore the fundamental limits of charge transport in topological semimetal niobium phosphide (NbP) nanoribbons down to approximately 6-nm widths, with industry-friendly top-down nanofabrication. The extracted NbP nanoribbon resistivity reaches 18 ± 4.1 μΩ cm at room temperature with an approximately 9-nm2 cross-sectional area, lower than that of conventional metals and semimetals with comparable size. The NbP nanoribbon resistivity decreases with decreasing width, unlike the classical behaviour of metals such as copper. This trend suggests a growing relative contribution of surface and edge states as the nanoribbon cross-section is reduced, despite a certain amount of disorder, including edge roughness. Our findings advance the understanding of size-dependent transport and scaling in this class of semimetals, offering a platform for nanoscale wires and interconnects in future nanoelectronics.

It has been revealed that H.S. and E.P. conceived of the core ideas and led the collaborations. H.S. fabricated nanoribbons and Hall bar devices, with support from D.Z. and T.P. H.S. measured room-temperature resistivity and breakdown of nanoribbons, and analysed the results with input from E.P., G.P., S.V. and X.B. H.S. also performed SEM and nanoribbon width and cross-sectional area extractions. S.A. took temperature-dependent transport measurements with input from Y.S. and H.S. A.F. carried out focused ion beam, STEM and four-dimensional STEM with support from A.J.B. and P.C.M. S.F.-W., X.W. and H.S. led thin-film deposition. H.B. and Y.Z. conducted density-functional-theory calculations with input from B.Y. M.J.H. and Y.D. led the ARPES measurements with input from Z.-X.S. T.P. took the X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy measurements. H.S. analysed the transport data with input from A.S., S.K., D.G.-G., B.Y. and E.P. H.S. wrote the paper, with major edits from E.P., and input from A.S., S.X.W., H.B., D.G.-G. and B.Y. All authors discussed the results and commented on the paper.

Sources indicate that a, High-angle annular dark-field (HAADF) image of the NbP (1.5 nm) nanoribbon with Nb (3.4 nm) seed layer. The electrically-conducting width of this device is ~12.5 nm. b, Magnified view of the nanocrystalline NbP layer and crystalline Nb seed, together with their corresponding Fast Fourier Transform (FFT), obtained from the boxed regions in panel a. c,d, Bright-field image (c) and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) elemental map (d) of the same device, showing distinct material compositions. In total, three NbP (1.5 nm) nanoribbons were examined by cross-sectional STEM. Across these samples, we observe consistent structural and compositional characteristics, including similar NbP crystallinity and sidewall oxidation, which support the scaling behaviour reported in this work. Additional STEM characterization was not performed on thicker NbP nanoribbons, as the thinnest nanoribbons are most relevant to the main conclusions of this study.

Recent findings suggest that a, HAADF image of the NbP (1.5 nm)/Nb (3.4 nm) nanoribbon with an electrically-conducting width of ~18 nm. b, Magnified view of the nanocrystalline NbP layer and crystalline Nb seed layer, together with their corresponding FFT, obtained from the boxed regions. c,d, Bright-field image (c) and EDS elemental map (d) of the same device, showing distinct material compositions of each region. e, EELS linescan profiles of Nb (blue) and P (red) normalized intensity as a function of position along the direction indicated in panel c. f-h, Representative nanobeam electron diffraction (NBED) patterns extracted from 4D-STEM data at probe positions within the sapphire substrate (f), Nb layer (g), and NbP layer (h), with indexed reflections confirming the distinct crystal structure of each region. i-k, Orientation template matching of the representative NBED pattern in f–h, for the sapphire substrate (i), Nb layer (j) and NbP layer (k). Coloured symbols indicate the local crystallographic orientation of the best-matching template for that pattern. l-n, Phase template matching of the same patterns for the sapphire substrate (l), Nb layer (m) and NbP layer (n).

a, Schematic of the scaling mechanism for conventional metals, with surface scattering and grain boundary scattering. b, As thickness and width of NbP are reduced, the conduction is consistent with the growing dominance of surface carriers, which are disorder-tolerant, with reduced scattering. The total sheet conductance in this case is a sum of the sheet conductance contributed from bulk carriers and surface carriers. c, For thick NbP, bulk carriers dominate the transport, and thus conventional scaling laws apply, with pronounced surface and grain boundary scattering. d, The Fuchs-Sondheimer (FS) and Mayadas-Shatzkes (MS) model fitting of 3.4 nm Nb seed layer, showing an excellent fit. The extracted resistivity with increasing width (W → ∞) is 56.3 μΩ∙cm, which matches the literature results. e, Sheet conductance (GNbP,□) of 1.5 nm NbP as a function of width (red curve), extracted from Fig. 2d of the main text. The sheet conductance from bulk carriers (extracted from Hall measurement) follows the conventional FS-MS scaling model (black dashed line), where the sheet conductance from surface carriers increases as the width decreases due to the increased surface area/volume ratio, as indicated by the purple dashed line. At this ultrathin thickness (1.5 nm), bulk carriers experience strong scattering, resulting in very small bulk carrier sheet conductance. f, GNbP,□ of 10 nm NbP as a function of width (blue curve). At NbP thickness of 10 nm, 3D bulk carriers and 2D top and bottom surface carriers contribute comparably to transport, as shown in Fig. 4b. At this thickness, as the nanoribbon width is reduced, the enhancement in surface conduction is insufficient to offset the increased scattering of bulk carriers. Consequently, bulk transport dominates in this regime, leading to a net reduction of sheet conductance (i.e., increased resistivity) with decreasing width, more similar to conventional metal wires. We note that there could be subtle differences in sidewall roughness and damage in the thicker nanoribbons compared to the thinner ones. See Supplementary Note 2 for the modelling details and more discussion.

In a recent development, a, Bulk Brillouin-zone schematic showing the two mirror planes and nodal rings from the band inversion. b, Representative band dispersion along Γ-S-M’, where the curves calculated without spin-orbit coupling (SOC) show the nodal-ring-related band inversion (plotted in green), and the curves calculated with SOC show the corresponding gap opening (black dashed lines). c, Real-space crystal view highlighting the helical states along the projected mirror line on the surface. d, Surface-state spectrum along \(\overline{\Gamma }\)-\(\overline{{\rm{X}}}\)-\(\overline{\Gamma }\)’, where the narrow Weyl-point window (grey shadow) hosts three pairs of helical states (indicated by arrows) that form the main part of the Fermi arcs, while remnant spin-split surface branches remain visible over a broader energy window (broad green shadow). Blue and red colours indicate the ‘± Sy’ spin polarization at opposite momenta, showing the helical feature. In summary, the narrow Fermi-arc structure is embedded inside a much broader nodal-ring-derived surface-state sector set by the band inversion. See Supplementary Note 7 for more discussion on bulk-topology hierarchy and topological surface-state interpretation.

a, Slab model along the [001] direction for the surface state calculations. Here, the 2 × 2 × 3 supercell is shown as an example. A 4.5 nm thick slab structure of the 1 × 1 × 4 supercell was used in the calculations. b,c, Surface band structures with Nb (b) and P (c) terminations along high-symmetry lines. Blue and red bands indicate the surface states of the Nb and P terminations, respectively. Bulk-projected states shown in pale blue are depicted as the background. The charge neutral point is set to 0 eV. d-f, Surface-projected Fermi surfaces with Nb (upper panels) and P (lower panels) terminations at 0 eV (d), −0.2 eV (e), and −0.4 eV (f). Darker colours represent larger contributions projected from the surface. Weyl points projected on the 2D Brillouin zone are shown as green and purple dots for opposite chirality. The constant energy cuts show surface-dominant open contours over a broad energy window, indicating that Weyl-derived surface bands persist even when the chemical potential is shifted deep into the hole-doped regime, which implies the robustness of the topological surface character. In addition, for the 4.5 nm thick NbP film, the top and bottom surface states exhibit minimal hybridization, except near the Weyl point projections where they meet each other. The Fermi-arc states remain largely unhybridized because they are well separated in momentum space. Even at momenta where they intersect, the resulting hybridization gap is negligible. See Supplementary Note 8 for the modelling details and more discussion.

a, Slab model from the NbP (001) film with thickness d = 1.5 nm and width W = 4.4 to 5.7 nm. b, The one-dimensional (1D) band structure of a W = 5 nm nanoribbon along ky direction. The edge projection is highlighted in purple to show the edge states, while the bulk states are shown in pale blue. Near EF, the edge-projected subbands form an electron-like pocket, consistent with the negative pedge values (panel f). c-e, The spin projection to Sx (c), Sy (d), and Sz (e) components, respectively, for the edge state. The blue and red represent opposite signs of spin polarization. These edge states exhibit a pronounced spin texture arising from strong spin-orbit coupling (SOC) in noncentrosymmetric NbP where Sx and Sz components are locked to the ky momentum in a Rashba-type SOC. This reduces the wavefunction overlap between counter-propagating modes, thereby suppressing the leading backscattering channel, which indicates high-mobility edge conduction. f, The carrier densities from edge (pedge) and 2D film (p2D) are extracted from linear fitting of the total ribbon density (p1D) by p1D = pedge + p2DW, at varying W. Wc denotes the cross-over width at which the edge carrier density would dominate the transport over the top and bottom surface carrier density. Here, Wc ≈ 0 indicates that the enhanced edge conduction of ultrathin films is not primarily driven by an increased edge carrier density. Instead, it is more plausibly attributed to an enhanced carrier mobility arising from reduced backscattering as the edge dimension approaches the quasi-1D limit. See more details in Supplementary Notes 2 and 8. g, Agreement between the nanoribbon fitting (\({p}_{2{\rm{D}}}^{{\rm{NR}}}\)) and that obtained from independent slab film calculations (\({p}_{2{\rm{D}}}^{{\rm{slab}}}\)) which corresponds to the d = 1.5 nm thickness in Supplementary Fig. 10. This agreement supports the self-consistency of our calculations across both the nanoribbon and thin-film geometries.

In a recent development, a, Temperature-dependent effective resistivity (ρeff) of NbP films with different thicknesses up to 90 nm, measured from Hall bar devices. These films have a 3.4 nm Nb seed layer, whose resistivity is measured separately (black symbols). b, Low-temperature limit (2-10 K) of panel a. The smallest superconducting transition temperature Tc (~2.2 K) is in the 3.4 nm Nb layer (black symbols), while higher Tc are observed in the NbP/Nb films, and Tc decreases monotonically with thicker NbP. The symbol colours follow the convention in panel a. c,d, Temperature-dependent sheet conductance (GNbP,□) (c) and resistivity (ρNbP) (d) for all NbP thicknesses, after subtracting the Nb seed contribution. e, ρNbP as a function of NbP thickness at 300 K and 10 K. For comparison, the ρNbP values of nanoribbons with the widest widths (Fig. 2d of the main text) are slightly higher than those from Hall measurements at 300 K, possibly due to process-induced damage during nanofabrication. f, Temperature-dependent ρeff of a ~5 nm-thick Nb control film, measured from a Hall bar device. The residual resistivity ratio (RRR) is 1.48, and the Tc is ~4.2 K. Inset: enlarged view of the low-temperature region. The presence of NbP appears to promote superconductivity in NbP/Nb films. The superconducting proximity effect is one plausible interpretation, although changes in disorder and enhanced inter-grain coupling (in the presence of NbP layer) could also contribute. We also cannot fully rule out the formation of an interfacial superconducting layer at the NbP/Nb interface. The NbP sheet conductance is obtained by subtracting the sheet conductance of the Nb layer (measured independently on control Nb films) from the total sheet conductance of the NbP/Nb stack. The extracted NbP resistivity is then obtained by dividing the NbP thickness by the NbP sheet conductance, i.e. ρNbP = dNbP/GNbP,□, where GNbP,□ = Gtot,□ - GNb,□ and Gtot,□ = dtot/ρeff, where Gtot,□ is the total sheet conductance of the NbP/Nb stack, dtot is the total stack thickness and ρeff is the measured effective resistivity (panel a). The GNbP,□ (panel c) represents the NbP sheet conductance after subtracting the independently-measured Nb seed contribution. Additional validation of the subtraction method using Pt/Nb stacks is provided in Supplementary Fig. 19. Control experiments using Pt/Nb stacks validate that the subtraction procedure itself does not generate an anomalous resistivity trend. Nevertheless, the conductance of the Nb seed layer within NbP/Nb stacks cannot be independently measured and it cannot be said, with absolute certainty, that its behaviour is identical to that of the separately measured Nb control film. Thus, the extracted NbP resistivity relies, by necessity, on the model used.

a-c, Hall resistance (Rxy) vs. magnetic field (B) measured at various temperatures for 3.4 nm Nb (a), 1.5 nm NbP (b), and 10 nm NbP (c). For the NbP films (b,c), the Nb seed layer contribution is subtracted at each corresponding temperature to extract NbP Hall response, using the same two-layer Hall conduction model described in the supplement. d, Effective three-dimensional carrier density (p3D) for all films, revealing opposite temperature-dependence: ultrathin 1.5 nm NbP shows an increasing p3D upon cooling, whereas both thicker NbP (10 nm) and Nb (3.4 nm) display decreasing p3D. (This figure is also included in the main text as Fig. 4d and is reproduced here for convenience). e, Effective hole mobility (μp) of the same films vs. temperature. NbP films exhibit a pronounced increase in mobility upon cooling due to suppressed phonon scattering, whereas the 3.4 nm Nb film shows only a slight rise in mobility, indicating that its transport remains strongly limited by surface scattering.

In a recent development, a-c, Longitudinal sheet resistance (Rxx) vs. magnetic field (B) measured at various temperatures for films of Nb seed layer (3.4 nm) (a), for NbP (1.5 nm) on the Nb seed (b), and for NbP (10 nm) on the Nb seed (c). All measurements were performed with the magnetic field applied perpendicular to the film plane and current direction. At low temperatures, all films exhibit a pronounced negative cusp near low field regions, arising from the interplay of superconducting fluctuations and weak antilocalization. d-e, Longitudinal sheet resistance (Rxx) vs. magnetic field (B) measured at 1.8 K for both 1.5 nm thick NbP (on 3.4 nm Nb seed layer) and for the Nb layer (3.4 nm) evaluated separately. Measurements were performed with B field perpendicular to the film plane and current direction (d), and with B applied in-plane (e). The superconducting transition temperatures are Tc ~ 6 K for the 1.5 nm NbP (on Nb) and ~2.2 K for the 3.4 nm Nb film (see Fig. 3d of the main text). The upper critical field Hc2, defined as the midpoint between the normal state resistance and zero resistance, is extracted. At 1.8 K, the out-of-plane critical field \({H}_{c2}^{\perp }\) is 2.2 T for NbP (1.5 nm) and 0.38 T for Nb (3.4 nm). The in-plane critical field at 1.8 K exceeds 9 T for NbP (1.5 nm) and reaches 4.44 T for Nb (3.4 nm). The superconducting coherence length estimates are provided in the supplement. The sense current used for Hall bar measurements is 0.5 mA, corresponding to a current density of ~0.1 MA/cm2 for the NbP (1.5 nm) film and ~0.15 MA/cm2 for the 3.4 nm Nb control, with the same 100 μm Hall bar device width. We note that this sense current is well below the superconducting critical current: even when we increased the sense current up to 10 mA, we were unable to suppress the superconducting state at 1.8 K.

Recent findings suggest that a, Cross-sectional HAADF STEM image of the alternating NbP/Nb multilayers grown on sapphire. b-d, Denoised nanobeam electron diffraction (NBED) patterns extracted from 4D-STEM data for all Nb layers (Nb layers 1-3) showing consistent body-centred cubic (bcc) diffraction symmetry with indexed reflections, confirming crystalline quality across all Nb layers. Scale bars: 0.5 Å−1. e, EDS line scan across the multilayer stack showing Nb (blue), P (red), and Al (light brown) as a function of position, integrated over a ~ 5nm wide region along the direction indicated by the yellow arrow in panel a, confirming periodic composition and abrupt elemental transitions at each NbP/Nb interface. f-h, denoised NBED patterns from NbP layers 1–3, displaying diffraction symmetry consistent with the NbP crystal structure with indexed reflections, consistent with uniform phase and crystallographic orientation throughout the multilayer stack. The diffraction spots become progressively broader from layer 1 to layer 3, suggesting a gradual decrease in crystalline coherence in NbP layers further from the substrate. This is further supported by the emergence of diffuse ring features in the Layer 3 diffraction pattern, indicative of increasing structural disorder.

Liverpool transfer news: Who is Sidy Barhama Ndiaye, the 16-year-old Senegalese phenomenon expected in 2028?

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (460 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Axel Clody | 26 Nov 2026 13:28.
  • In a recent development, liverpool may have found their next great Senegalese talent.
  • However, Liverpool fans will have to be patient, as the young Senegalese cannot move to England until January 2028.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Axel Clody | 26 Nov 2026 13:28.

In a recent development, liverpool may have found their next great Senegalese talent. The Premier League club have reportedly reached a verbal agreement to sign Sidy Barhama Ndiaye, a 16-year-old winger who presently plays for Diambars.

However, Liverpool fans will have to be patient, as the young Senegalese cannot move to England until January 2028.

The news was revealed by Fabrizio Romano, who confirmed that a verbal agreement exists between the two parties.

It has been revealed that having already been given a trial by Liverpool in the summer of 2025, Ndiaye reportedly convinced the club's scouts, who have now secured an option on his arrival. Born on 31 December 2009, he will turn 18 at the end of 2027, which is a requirement for a move to England.

According to recent reports, ??? Liverpool have verbally agreed deal to sign 16 year old winger Sidy Barhama Ndiaye, here we go! Senegalese talent to join in January 2028, when he turns 18. Ndiaye was already at Liverpool on trial in 2025 and ready to become #LFC player for future. https://t.co/DrBIfNkPJR.

Recent findings suggest that A product of Diambars, one of the most renowned academies in Senegal, Sidy Barhama Ndiaye plays mainly on the right but can also operate on the left. He first caught the eye at the 2025 Under-17 Africa Cup of Nations, played when he was only 15, before continuing to progress with Senegal's youth teams.

In a recent development, his main qualities are his pace, his explosiveness and his ability to beat an opponent one on one. Very direct when receiving the ball, he likes to provoke, accelerate and create openings. He also has a degree of efficiency in the final ball, as he again demonstrated at the Under-17 World Cup.

In a recent development, during Senegal's 9-0 thrashing of Cuba, the young winger scored one goal and provided two assists. The performance helped to boost his reputation among European observers and scouts.

The comparison with Sadio Mane comes naturally around the young Senegalese.

Besides his origins, Ndiaye shares with his illustrious elder an attacking profile built on pace, penetration and the ability to make a difference on the wings. And if Liverpool, who benefited from Mane's talent for six seasons, complete the deal, that comparison will be unavoidable.

It has been revealed that however, there is still a long way to go before he can be expected to play at Anfield. Between now and January 2028, Ndiaye will have to continue to progress at Diambars and confirm the promise shown with Senegal's youth teams.

Liverpool, for their part, have already taken a position on a player they want to integrate into their long-term project.

Nottingham Forest vs. Chelsea: How to watch, date, time, live stream and TV channel for Premier League clash

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (390 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Darren Plant | 26 Nov 2026 13:37.
  • Nottingham Forest and Chelsea will attempt to earn a much-needed boost in the Premier League when they square off on Friday night.
  • Despite seven points separating these teams in the Premier League table, the home side are arguably the favourites to prevail from this fixture.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Darren Plant | 26 Nov 2026 13:37.

Nottingham Forest and Chelsea will attempt to earn a much-needed boost in the Premier League when they square off on Friday night.

Despite seven points separating these teams in the Premier League table, the home side are arguably the favourites to prevail from this fixture.

Here, Sports Mole provides details of how to tune into the contest.

The Premier League match will kick off at 8pm, UK time, on Saturday.

This Premier League game between Nottingham Forest and Chelsea will be held at the City Ground, the home stadium of Forest.

Last season's corresponding fixture ended in a 3-0 victory for Chelsea, albeit in a game where Forest - then with Ange Postecoglou at the helm - squandered a number of opportunities.

The Premier League contest will be available on Sky Sports Main Event and Sky Sports Premier League for viewers in the UK.

Sky customers can access the Premier League match on Sky Go and on the Sky Sports app, while it is also available via Now TV's Sports membership.

Sky Sports will show highlights, including any goals which have been scored, on their social media and YouTube channels, as well as on their dedicated app.

Meanwhile, those wishing to watch highlights on Match of the Day will have to wait until Saturday evening, with the programme starting at 10.30pm.

Both teams head into this fixture with question marks over their physicality, an matter which Oliver Glasner addressed in his pre-match press conference.

Forest begin the latest batch of games sitting in 17th position in the Premier League table, but they can move into 14th place with victory on Friday night.

Eight teams - including Chelsea - possess a worse defensive record than Forest, emphasising the feeling that they could swiftly move up the standings if they resolve their complications in the final third.

On the back of three defeats in four matches and with 20 goals conceded in 11 games, Chelsea will be perceived to be ideal opponents for Forest.

While Chelsea have the opportunity to move into fifth place, they are highly likely to end the weekend in the bottom half of the table should they lose in the East Midlands.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There have been some dark days in the post-Sir Alex Ferguson era but this was up there with the very worst of them: the kind of performance that gets a manager sacked, the kind of display that points to a fundamental disconnect, the kind of occasion that leaves you thinking Manchester United are as far away as they have ever been.

When players seem so averse to doing the very basics, such as running, and the club habitually have such trouble attracting the right profiles and personalities, it is hard to escape the feeling that saying goodbye to another manager is going to do little more than paper over the many cracks at Old Trafford.

But, watching this, you had to think Michael Carrick will do well to limp on as far as Sunday, when United face Bournemouth at Old Trafford.

And that was before we had heard the United captain, Bruno Fernandes, appearing to call out the manager’s tactics just a week on from the last show of public dissent from a player, when Lisandro Martínez attacked the Old Trafford board. If only these players were as good at talking on the pitch.

At the final whistle, Carrick walked over to the 700-strong group of United supporters, held up both hands in apology on no fewer than seven occasions and then walked off down the tunnel without looking in the direction of any of his players.

There were shades of Ole Gunnar Solskjaer at Watford in November 2021, when he also held up his hands in apology before being sacked 24 hours later.

Recent findings suggest that in that instance, United fans booed Solskjaer. Carrick at least received some polite applause from the fans, who are a smart bunch and know the club’s problems extend far beyond the man in the dugout. Still, it is always the manager who pays the price. Solskjaer said he knew at half-time he was toast and Carrick is now under real threat himself – and seemingly at loggerheads with his captain.

Sources indicate that fernandes’s criticism of United’s set-up and approach was cutting and a direct attack on his manager and backroom team. “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man to man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence,” the United captain noted.

Sources indicate that carrick has been telling us for weeks that he and his squad are together, that the team are not too far away, that it is all about small margins. He even described Sunday’s 1-1 draw at Leeds as a “fresh start”. But Como blew the lid off any pretence of that being the case. Even by the standards of this season to date, though, what unfolded here in the rain in Lombardy was shocking to witness.

Como, inspired by the outstanding Nico Paz, were every bit as good as United – who have won just two of 11 games this season – were a pitiful mess.

That in itself told you a lot about these players and this team and it set the tone for what was to follow: a masterclass in incompetence and indifference. There have only been four worse results in United’s European history, although you will struggle to find a poorer performance than this.

Michael Carrick has insisted there is not a “toxic culture” at Manchester United in the wake of scathing criticism from former manager Erik ten Hag of the Old Trafford hierarchy and player power at the club.

The current United manager – who is under pressure after the club’s worst start to a season for 40 years – also believes he has the backing of the United board, despite Ten Hag accusing Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s Ineos regime of a series of “broken promises”.

In an interview with The Athletic, Ten Hag blamed Ratcliffe and his executives for fuelling a “toxic culture” by giving power to players and failing to back him on disciplinary matters relating to Marcus Rashford, Jadon Sancho and other first-teamers.

But Carrick said he had not encountered any toxicity since taking over from Ruben Amorim in January and suggested United’s last two outings, a 1-1 draw against Leeds United and a 2-0 defeat to Atlético Madrid, underlined the camaraderie in the group.

“Since I came back, the players and the staff have given us everything that they could give,” Carrick stated before Wednesday’s Champions League clash against Cesc Fàbregas’s Como in northern Italy, where he is battling an injury and illness crisis.

“We’ve had some good performances. We’ve had some performances that we want to do better and we can improve on. We’ve made some mistakes.

“But I have to say, the type of performance put into the weekend and for large parts against Atlético, there’s a lot of togetherness there. There’s a lot of will and determination to do better and wanting to do it for each other, which is notable.”.

And an uninspiring draw at Elland Road on Sunday did little to settle the rising tide of discontent within the United fanbase.

When asked for his team news, the first words that came from the United head coach’s mouth were: “Right, bit of mixed bag to be honest.” That was not a great sign, and Carrick will be without Martínez, Kobbie Mainoo, Luke Shaw, Ayden Heaven, Marcus Rashford, Benjamin Sesko and Patrick Dorgu, who are injured, while Leny Yoro serves a suspension following his red card against Atlético Madrid.

The abundantly talented Argentine No 10 Nico Paz will feature, however, and he will be keen to showcase his talents in the Champions League.

Como have ascended from Serie B to Europe’s top table in three seasons (and from bankruptcy in nine) under Cesc Fàbregas’ watchful eye. The Spaniard is a minority owner and shareholder of the club, but as head coach he has introduced an incisive, possession-based style of play which contains hints of the managerial greats under whom he played: Arsène Wenger, Pep Guardiola, José Mourinho, Vicente del Bosque, Antonio Conte etc.

Industry News: Amid protests, France's rising debt costs threaten stability

📅 06 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (988 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Deeply indebted, politically trapped in a standoff between extremes and led by a government without a parliamentary majority: These are the defining features of France's current predicament.
  • If, in response to nationwide protests, the government prepares to provide €4 billion ($4.48 billion) in low-interest loans to renovate schools by 2030 and allocate a further €1 billion to universities by 2029, it is promising money the state simply does not have.
  • France's public debt stands at around 120% of gross domestic product (GDP).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Deeply indebted, politically trapped in a standoff between extremes and led by a government without a parliamentary majority: These are the defining features of France's current predicament.

If, in response to nationwide protests, the government prepares to provide €4 billion ($4.48 billion) in low-interest loans to renovate schools by 2030 and allocate a further €1 billion to universities by 2029, it is promising money the state simply does not have.

France's public debt stands at around 120% of gross domestic product (GDP). By comparison, Germany's debt-to-GDP ratio is roughly 65%, despite its €600 billion investment package for infrastructure and defense.

Germany still enjoys the highest possible AAA credit rating. France, by contrast, is rated AA, A+ or Aa3, depending on the credit agency. While Germany's outlook is consistently rated as stable, several agencies have assigned France a negative outlook.

Sources indicate that as a result, the French government must pay higher interest rates on its borrowing than Berlin. The risk premium over German government bonds, known as the spread, is now at its highest level since the financial crisis. France pays nearly 1.6 percentage points more in interest than Germany on 10-year bonds.

The spread acts as a kind of "fever gauge" for bond markets, explained Friedrich Heinemann, an economist at the Leibniz Center for European Economic Research (ZEW) in Mannheim.

Industry observers note that "This fever gauge then forces a change of course. If the spread rises too sharply, France's financing conditions come under pressure, and anyone in France who needs a loan has to pay higher interest rates. Banks then get into trouble, and the crisis escalates further," Heinemann told DW.

"This could then slide toward a financial crisis, which would finally send a clear signal to everyone: Things cannot continue like this unless you are prepared to risk a genuine economic collapse," he stated.

Landry Charrier, a researcher at the University of Bonn's Center for Advanced Security, Strategic and Integration Studies, however, does not expect France's debt-fueled spending spree to end anytime soon.

Industry observers note that "French people are aware of the country's high public debt. But debt remains an abstract concept if its consequences are barely felt in everyday life. According to INSEE [the French national statistics agency — Editor's note], 56% of the population receive more in government benefits and services than they pay in taxes and social contributions. The majority therefore have a tangible interest in maintaining the status quo," Charrier told DW.

For more than half a century, France has regularly spent more than it collects in tax revenue. The last time it balanced its national budget was in 1974.

France last paid a similarly high-risk premium at the end of 2011, during the eurozone debt crisis. What is particularly striking is how quickly it has risen: Since June 2026, the spread over German government bonds has more than doubled.

The main driver is not so much the general level of interest rates. Rather, it's the growing risk premium investors demand in response to high debt levels, political instability, large budget deficits and the recent unrest.

Sources indicate that the higher the interest rates, the larger the share of the national budget that must be devoted to debt servicing alone. France is expected to pay more than €79 billion in interest on its total public debt in 2026. That figure is projected to exceed €91 billion in 2027 and could reach between €125 billion and €132 billion by 2030.

These figures include the costs incurred by social security funds and local authorities. The central government's interest bill alone is currently estimated at €62.6 billion by the Agence France Tresor, a French Treasury agency.

In the coming years, France will have to refinance large amounts of outstanding bonds that were issued when interest rates were at historic lows. At the same time, the country's substantial budget deficit means it must take on additional debt.

Recent findings suggest that the trend of rising interest costs is also affecting Germany. The ZEW's Heinemann has calculated that German interest payments are likely to increase sharply by the early 2030s.

"For the federal government alone, which has so far paid around €30 billion, the figure will triple within a few years as both debt and interest rates rise. And it won't stop there — it will exceed €90 billion. Reaching €100 billion in annual interest payments in the federal budget is then no longer far off," warned the economist.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

In France, however, economic realities seem to have little impact on political debate. Both the far-right National Rally (RN) and the far-left France Unbowed (LFI) are campaigning on costly promises.

Sources indicate that RN leader Marine Le Pen, for example, wants to reinstate the retirement age of 62 while promising €140 billion in savings. Jean-Luc Melenchon, LFI's leader, has even suggested that government bonds held by the French central bank should be "thrown into the fire.".

"Nobody will ever notice they've disappeared," he has claimed.

For Heinemann, this is "a good example of radical parties on both the right and the left simply telling economic fairy tales.".

Their common message, he said, is that "there is a way out of this mess that requires neither fiscal consolidation nor painful cuts.".

Charrier is convinced that many French people have yet to grasp the seriousness of the situation.

"The euro has made it easier for France to access cheap financing and has long softened the pressure to adjust," he pointed out.

Industry observers note that "In the past, currency devaluations [of the French franc — Editor's note] made economic imbalances immediately felt through declining purchasing power and rising prices. Today, that warning signal is missing. This has created the illusion that necessary adjustments can be postponed indefinitely," Charrier remarked.

This article was originally written in German.

  • Both beaten 5-1 last weekend, Frosinone and Parma will aim to bounce back when they clash at Stadio Benito Stirpe on Saturday.
  • Despite suffering consecutive defeats for the first time this term, the hosts are still 12 points above their visitors in the Serie A standings.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Jonathan O'Shea | 26 Nov 2026 13:47.

Both beaten 5-1 last weekend, Frosinone and Parma will aim to bounce back when they clash at Stadio Benito Stirpe on Saturday.

Despite suffering consecutive defeats for the first time this term, the hosts are still 12 points above their visitors in the Serie A standings.

Frosinone made an unexpectedly strong start to their latest comeback campaign, scoring freely while winning six of their first 11 fixtures after returning to Serie A.

However, Massimiliano Alvini's attack-minded side then suffered a rare setback, going down 1-0 to Cagliari, before they were well beaten just after the international break.

Two goals down within 20 minutes, the Canarini continued to fly forward, but they never really recovered and ultimately lost 5-1 to AC Milan at San Siro.

In fact, Frosinone have only claimed two points on the road since beating Fiorentina at the end of August, so their form at Stadio Stirpe has kept them tucked inside the top half.

After narrowly losing their first home fixture against Juventus, they have since won all of the next five, so confidence should still be high when lowly Parma come to town.

While their promoted hosts sit seventh in Serie A, Parma are hovering above the relegation zone with just eight points on the board.

Like Frosinone, they were thumped 5-1 last week, as Roma stormed to victory at Stadio Tardini, with Capocannoniere leader Donyell Malen helping himself to four goals.

That was the Gialloblu's eighth defeat from their first 12 league games, and the recent hiring of their second-highest Serie A scorer has hardly had an impact.

Alberto Gilardino has only celebrated one win since succeeding Carlos Cuesta, who kept the Emilian club afloat last term, but that lone success did come on the road.

Following a run of six straight away defeats, Parma recently beat Atalanta 3-0 in Bergamo, so they will aim to claim more points when they head south on Saturday.

Now trailing Malen in the race to be crowned Italy's top scorer, Frosinone striker Antonio Raimondo is still sidelined by injury - and his deputy is also unavailable.

Daniel Birligea bagged a brace against Lecce before scoring for Romania in their recent Nations League camp, but he strained a hamstring in Milan and has been ruled out for the next few weeks.

So, it remains to be seen whether Alvini selects support forwards Fares Ghedjemis, Romano Schmid and Giorgi Kvernadze - each of whom have provided four Serie A assists - or Slovak centre-forward Tomas Bobcek to lead the hosts' attack.

On the absence front, Florian Grillitsch has yet to recover from a thigh problem, but left-back Gabriele Bracaglia can return after serving a one-match ban.

While Parma will welcome back Abdoulaye Ndiaye from suspension, Argentine striker David Romero is still ruled out by a serious shoulder injury; defensive duo Diego Carlos (thigh) and Dominik Drobnic (foot) are also doubts.

In Romero's absence, Simone Lontani could partner El Bilal Toure, but Nesta Elphege is also a contender after scoring the Gialloblu's lone goal against Roma.

Frosinone possible starting lineup:.

Palmisani; Oyono, Monterisi, Calvani, Bracaglia; Masini, Calo; Ghedjemis, Schmid, Kvernadze; Bobcek.

Parma possible starting lineup:.

Daffara; Delprato, Troilo, Ndiaye; Britschgi, Fabbian, Sierro, Keita, Valeri; Elphege, Toure.

Frosinone can arrest their decline with another home win, as Parma are in grim form and could face a long fight to avoid the drop.

Notably, the Canarini tend to start fast - scoring a league-high 11 goals inside the first 30 minutes - while their visitors have yet to score before the half-hour mark.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Scottish football chiefs have extended the consultation period for its prepares to encourage the selection of more youngsters “with the intention of a comprehensive proposal within the first quarter of 2027” amid concerns from some major clubs.

The Scottish Football Association invited all 42 league clubs to a summit at St Andrews in early September, where they unveiled a package of proposals aimed at securing the future of the sport in Scotland.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

The SFA wants a minimum of two Scottish under-21 players to be selected by each team in a Scottish Cup tie and for two Scottish under-21 players to be picked by each team in the Premier Sports Cup, starting from the 2027/28 campaign.

From next season as well, the SFA has also suggested under-21 players be on the pitch for an average of 60 minutes per game, across the season, in the Premiership, equating to six per cent of available minutes.

Led by recently-appointed chief football officer Craig Mulholland, the SFA had hoped to put some of their aims to a vote at the Scottish Professional Football League annual general meeting this month. With a downward trajectory of young Scottish players being selected in the Premiership over the past ten years, Mulholland stated in September that “we need to act now, otherwise we could end up finding ourselves in a crisis at some point in the future”.

The fear is that Scotland risks falling behind similarly-sized nations and will fail to qualify for major tournaments, while Premiership clubs were told by external firm Twenty First Group that they are leaving £40 million on the table in potential revenue by not placing more faith in academy players.

Nevertheless, The Scotsman understands that some of the SFA’s proposals have been met with scepticism from clubs across the leagues and the governing body has extended the consultation period “into the Upcoming Year” to continue dialogue on the best way forward.

A statement from the Scottish Football Association read: “The Scottish FA has been encouraged by the productive dialogue with clubs regarding proposals to harness opportunities for young homegrown talent.

“The most recent discussions have spawned a range of additional potential innovations that all parties agree will require further consultation in order to present a consolidated package of recommendations to an SPFL member vote.

“The passion we all have for Scottish football has been demonstrated by the public debate sparked since the all-club meeting in St Andrews, when the reality of our domestic game’s standing in respect of playing time for under-21 players compared to the rest of Europe was made clear.

“We will continue to engage in dialogue with the aim of delivering a proposal that will achieve the stated objective of improving opportunities for young homegrown players to fulfil their potential at the top end of the Scottish professional game.

“It is an objective everyone benefits from: players, clubs, supporters and Scotland national teams.

“We have therefore agreed that the consultation process will continue into the New Year with the intention of a comprehensive proposal going to SPFL members within the first quarter of 2027, in time for the start of William Hill SPFL season 2027-28.

“The Scottish FA General Meeting to vote on the complementary Scottish Gas Men’s Scottish Cup proposals will now follow a similar timetable.

“Given the implications for our game, and our young talent, it is imperative that we take the necessary time to get those proposals right.”.

Speared Hearts’ craziness goes on as Gorgie boys give Monaco something to drop off at Louvre

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1047 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Scotsman

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Eight goals at Dens Park is one thing.
  • Recent findings suggest that the price the Hearts fans might have to pay for such swashbuckling play was also demonstrated.
  • Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Eight goals at Dens Park is one thing. Going toe-to-toe with French aristocrats and being beaten, cruelly, at the death is quite another. Hearts’ growing reputation as the great entertainers was nevertheless burnished here in thrilling fashion.

Recent findings suggest that the price the Hearts fans might have to pay for such swashbuckling play was also demonstrated. Defensive fragility was all too apparent, including at the end when substitute Mamadou Coulibaly brushed off a challenge in midfield and threaded the ball through for Folarin Balogun to score his second and the night’s decisive goal. We were already into the final minute of the four added on at the end of a quite breathless European tie.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

It has been revealed that mon Dieu! What a match. AS Monaco won’t forget this trip to Scotland, and a vibrant Tynecastle, in a hurry. As for the hosts, they remain just about alive in the Conference League.

The point they were deprived in heartbreaking fashion would have made such a difference. As good as Monaco are, it wasn’t as if Hearts were undone by a moment of genius, which makes it harder to bear. The hosts also had chances to score their own third goal and were angered when referee Daniel Schlager waved away penalty appeals when substitute Josh McPake ended up in a heap after Jordan Teze’s challenge.

Perhaps the home supporters will simply have to put up with see-sawing emotions in a season that’s already shaping up to be one of the craziest in the club’s history. Perhaps defensive slackness, although costly, must simply be endured if goals continue to flow at the other end, especially ones as sensational as Hearts fans were treated to here. Drop them off in the Louvre on your way home, Monaco.

Jordi Altena’s opener was declared a “potential” goal of the season by the always judicious Tynecastle Tannoy announcer. Just as well because a better one was just around the corner. Sabah Kerjota’s curler on the stroke of half time was an immaculate finish that Lukas Hradecky, the experienced keeper, just had to stand rooted to his spot and admire.

Altena’s strike was not quite in the same unsavable part of the goal but it was still breathtaking in its execution. Kerjota, the little Albanian livewire, also played a part in it. His free-kick looked to be going in until Hradecky pushed the ball against the post. Claudio Braga made sure the ball was recycled and played it back to Kerjota, who passed it inside to Altena. The Dutchman is fast becoming a Tynecastle favourite. No wonder when he can strike a ball like this. Hradecky was left flapping at the air beneath his bar.

Since going 5-0 down to Falkirk after 47 minutes earlier this month at Tynecastle, Hearts had scored 10 unanswered goals. This was the 11th. The response was always coming. This was AS Monaco after all. They might be struggling presently in Ligue 1 but how can they be they be written off? The team remains packed full of talent. This was not the shadow side Hearts might have hoped to face. Eric Dier, the England international, was present and correct as was former Arsenal player – and Donald Trump’s friend - Balogun.

Sources indicate that monaco were the ones raising a quizzical French eyebrow at the home team sheet. Due to much publicised injury problems and lack of adequate club-trained academy players, Hearts couldn’t even fill the bench.

According to recent reports, matthew Gillies stepped in for his first senior start in midfield. Unless Monaco were familiar with Stenhousemuir's opening matches of this season, the talented 19-year-old might have been something of a mystery to them. The same applies to Finlay Pollock, who is something of a mystery to Hearts fans as well.

Recent findings suggest that pollock came on towards the end for his first Hearts appearance since 2024. The 22-year-old has been out on loan at East Fife and Raith Rovers in between times. He was given the last nine minutes in place of a drained Kerjota. The whole team, including substitutes, looked shattered at the end but they had contributed to a game that will live long in the memory. There was the drama of an overturned penalty for Hearts in the second half after an alleged handball by substitute Mathys Detourbet as well as the sight of Beau Reus galloping up field for a corner in the final seconds.

The visitors’ first goal of the night saw Balogun do the necessary – and no more - from the penalty spot after Stuart Findlay had clipped the heels of the dangerous Matthis Abline.

Recent findings suggest that there was some dismay among home fans about Reus’ lack of movement. Balogun’s penalty lacked conviction and certainly wasn’t placed in the corner. Far from it. Nevertheless, it brought Monaco level. The French side took heart although they didn’t have it all their own way. Abline was booked for a foul on Laurent Mendy as Hearts forced the visitors into sometimes desperate measures.

Monaco did though take the lead for the first time in the night five minutes before half time after Edan Diop took advantage of a slack ball from Altena following a throw-in. After playing a one-two with Balogun, he slipped the ball beyond Reus.

Sources indicate that gillies was showing his worth in midfield. He might have had a goal to tell his pals about had Pierre Landry Kabore not taken the ball off his foot as he was preparing to unleash a shot from the edge of the box. Kabore, following his brace against Dundee, was in frisky form but often got a little too excited and forgot the basics, such as avoiding running into teammates.

Industry observers note that gillies was withdrawn at half time for Blair Spittal, back from injury and desperate to play a part. He also took the captain’s armband from McCart and helped drive Hearts on. Sadly, his and others’ efforts were in vain on an agonising night for the hosts.

Latest Update: ‘It’s very beautiful’ - Monaco applaud Hearts as Vrancken insists cruel defeat ‘doesn’t make a difference’

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Wouter Vrancken has stressed Hearts’ objective remains the same despite conceding a last-minute goal that led to an agonising defeat against AS Monaco at Tynecastle.
  • Hearts’ hopes of reaching the knockout stage rest on winning their last two Conference League matches against Bosnian side Borac Banja Luca and Cypriot team Pafos, probably by high-scoring margins.
  • Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Wouter Vrancken has stressed Hearts’ objective remains the same despite conceding a last-minute goal that led to an agonising defeat against AS Monaco at Tynecastle.

Hearts’ hopes of reaching the knockout stage rest on winning their last two Conference League matches against Bosnian side Borac Banja Luca and Cypriot team Pafos, probably by high-scoring margins.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

The Tynecastle manager was not giving up on anything after the 3-2 loss, with United States World Cup star Folarin Balogun scoring the winning goal in the final seconds of added time.

In a recent development, hearts had taken the lead after a sensational strike from Jordi Altena on 15 minutes. A penalty from Balogun levelled things before the visitors took the lead with a goal from Edam Diop five minutes before half time. Sabah Kerjota scored the goal of the night on the stroke of half-time after curling in with his left foot to leave everything to play for in the second half.

“I think the point doesn't make a difference,” mentioned Vrancken. “There's also something that really was pleasing for me is that when it was 2-2, we still wanted to go (for the win).

In a recent development, "You saw also when it was a throw-in, we wanted to do it fast, we wanted to go for the win. Against a side like this, in the situation we're in, I am so really proud of this also.

"Three points would make a difference," he added. "Zero or one point doesn't make a difference towards the next games, so you have to win the next games. One point or no points doesn't change anything in the next games.”.

The Belgian stressed his pride in his players and reiterated that Hearts were missing nine injured players as well as Leart Kabashi and Eduardo Ageu, who were not named in the European squad. He did, however, lament the lack of concentration that saw them concede so late in the game after 93-and-a-half minutes of lung-busting effort. He was also unhappy that Hearts were not cute enough to stop Monaco in their tracks as they broke free for the winning goal. Substitute Finlay Pollock had the chance to clip Mamadou Coulibaly’s heels before the midfielder played in Balogun. Ruthlessness might be something Hearts are lacking at this level. A reporter pointed out that it was a cruel way to lose a match.

“It did feel like this,” mentioned Vrancken. “But at the same time, we have to learn in that situation because I think until then we were really solid about giving chances away. And I expect more from guys who come in from the side (substitutes).

“We can win it with a fresh player and in the middle we can win it with a fresh player. Or you make a foul somewhere to keep the result - I expect this. This is like battling for the team, as I call it.

Recent findings suggest that “We have to do better there,” he added. “But the biggest thing, of course, is to be really proud of what performance we put on the park today, because it's against a really good side. Knowing that we have still nine injuries - I will name it - and we have a lot of players not on the European list today and still do this against that team. I'm really proud of what we did.”.

Sources indicate that he hailed the quality of his side’s goals. “You see also the confidence those guys have. This is what we wanted after the weekend, of course - that you take some confidence from the dynamics of what we did there. I think the conviction around the box was there, in both boxes actually. It's an key thing to take with us towards the next games coming, especially in this run of games.”.

Industry observers note that hearts host Celtic, who beat them 7-1 last month, at Tynecastle on Sunday. Vrancken is firmly in the belief that his side have their mojo back following this and the 5-2 defeat to Falkirk earlier this month. Hearts have since beaten Dundee 8-0 and been edged out by Monaco in a five-goal thriller. “We have played two good games and two good performances against good sides, especially today,” he remarked. “And now you have the confidence. But we are still playing against a good side on Sunday with only two days' rest, so we have to manage fatigue and make sure that we are as fresh as possible again to make up for something a few weeks ago, especially because it's an at-home game.”.

Recent findings suggest that monaco manager Filipe Luis, meanwhile, denied that relief was the primary emotion after leaving it so late to collect three points. “It is not relief, we compete to win,” he noted. “We had an amazing opportunity to win tonight but we had a tough opponent.

In a recent development, “They scored two unbelievable goals,” he added. “You almost need to applaud them. When a team scores two goals like this it is almost nobody’s fault. They are two fantastic goals. Honestly, it’s very beautiful.”.

It has been revealed that he spoke admiringly of the atmosphere. “I played against Celtic (with Atletico Madrid) in 2011 I think in the Europa League,” he stated. “We are lucky to have the opportunity to play these types of games in different countries. It is so intense. I am happy to have had this opportunity to be here tonight – and happy with the result.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Colombian’s late header ends Celtic’s 23-year Portuguese hoodoo in gritty Torreense triumph.

Celtic clinched a vital 2-1 Europa League victory over second-tier outfit Torreense, thanks to an 84th-minute header from substitute Camilo Duran that ended the Scottish champions' 23-and-a-half-year wait for an away win on Portuguese soil.

Played nearly 50 miles away from Torreense’s 2,431-capacity home at Estadio Manuel Marques, which fails to meet UEFA stadium criteria, the 24,000-seater Municipal Stadium in Leiria was dominated by roughly 4,000 travelling Celtic supporters, making up two-thirds of the crowd. Despite the partisan backing, Martin O’Neill’s men made remarkably hard work of overcoming a side sitting 13th in Portugal’s second division with just two league wins from their opening ten matches.

Sources indicate that there is an old adage in European football that fortunes earned by accident are rarely retained by design. For 45 disjointed minutes, Celtic offered a textbook demonstration of the principle. Handed an early advantage through the sort of comical defending usually reserved for Scottish clubs on their continental travels, Martin O’Neill’s side promptly retreated into their shell, allowing Portuguese second-tier minnows Torreense to restore parity and seize the initiative before the interval.

According to recent reports, celtic’s precarious Europa League campaign was balanced on a knife-edge. Having opened their league-phase campaign with three consecutive defeats before salvaging a breathless 3-2 victory over Beşiktaş in Glasgow earlier this month, O’Neill’s men arrived in central Portugal languishing in 32nd place.

Anything less than maximum points against a Torreense side operating in the lower reaches of Liga Portugal 2, yet remarkably seated 19th in this competition with six points following last season’s improbable Taça de Portugal triumph, threatened to render Celtic’s remaining fixtures against Omonia, Marseille, and Union Saint-Gilloise an exercise in mathematical futility.

Industry observers note that O’Neill had cautioned on the eve of the tie that his squad lacked the pedigree to indulge in complacency. Initially, however, the evening appeared set to unfold with uncharacteristic smoothness for the Scottish champions.

Restored to the European squad as an injury replacement for Mika Baur, Jota marked his return to his homeland with immediate industry down the left flank. Inside nine minutes, the winger collected possession near the by-line and whipped a low, enticing delivery into the six-yard box. With Yang Hyun-jun hovering intently at the back post, Torreense full-back Javi Vázquez panicked under pressure, slicing his attempted clearance past his own goalkeeper and into the net.

It was a moment of extreme generosity, yet Celtic proved remarkably ungrateful recipients. Rather than using their early cushion to assert authority, the visitors lapsed into a passive, defensive shell. Though Celtic commanded the majority of possession, they managed to invite pressure rather than alleviate it.

In a recent development, torreense, a club steeped in modest provincial history rather than continental glamour, sensed the vulnerability. Vázquez nearly atoned for his earlier mistake in the 17th minute with a venomous, low free-kick from a narrow angle that required hasty defensive intervention. Two minutes later, the equaliser duly arrived, born of Celtic’s chronic inability to clear their lines.

Given acres of space 20 yards from goal, midfielder Álex Alfaro unleashed a fierce drive that crashed against the underside of Sam Johnstone’s crossbar. As the ball dropped invitingly inside the penalty area, Celtic’s backline froze. Kieran Tierney’s tentative, lofted clearance succeeded only in teeing up Dany Jean, and the forward exhibited admirable composure to dart past Colby Donovan and drill a low finish beyond Johnstone’s reach.

According to recent reports, jota remained Celtic’s sole reliable source of invention. Celtic’s solitary threat to reclaim the lead prior to the break arrived on the stroke of half-time, when the Portuguese star's deep cross was hooked back across the face of goal by Luke McCowan, only for Kasper Høgh to arrive a fraction too late to apply the finishing touch.

Recent findings suggest that jota nearly restored the lead within seconds of the restart, only for his attempted dink to be gathered by a scrambling Adriel. But as the hour mark approached, Celtic’s frustration grew.

Former Hearts striker Musa Drammeh nearly dealt a massive blow to their hopes of progressing to the knockout stages by shrugging off a feeble challenge before dragging a golden chance narrowly wide of the far post.

It has been revealed that james Forrest took over from the impressive Jota in the closing stages and the substitution proved to be a masterstroke. With Celtic seemingly sleepwalking toward a damaging result, Forrest swung a pinpoint cross in from the right, and Duran peeled away at the back post to power a downward header past Adriel. It was the Colombian’s 15th goal of a remarkable campaign, once again rescuing his side.

Recent findings suggest that mcCowan missed a late one-on-one opportunity to add a touch of gloss to the scoreline in the 89th minute, seeing his tame finish saved by Adriel’s boot. However, it did not matter. For the first time since O’Neill’s side triumphed at Boavista in April 2003, Celtic left Iberian soil victorious.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Carter White | 26 Nov 2026 13:52.

Aiming to remain unbeaten at home in the league this season, promotion-hunting Birmingham City host struggling Bolton Wanderers at St Andrew's @ Knighthead Park in the Championship on Saturday afternoon.

Blues were the latest side to take advantage of Burnley's Turf Moor misery on Wednesday night, whilst the Wanderers suffered defeat on their own patch by West Bromwich Albion.

As has been the case after each of their three Championship defeats so far this season, Birmingham City bounced back from last weekend's Stoke City disappointment by claiming three points, this time at the expense of crisis-hit Burnley.

Chris Davies's side have already equalled the number of away victories that they managed across the entirety of last season (6) courtesy of August Priske's seventh league goal of the term and an own goal from Clarets winger Jaydon Banel at Turf Moor.

Following seven wins from their past nine second-tier contests, Birmingham are occupying fourth position in the Championship table, three points behind current pacesetters Middlesbrough and Stoke.

Apart from a 6-1 battering by Brentford in the EFL Cup, Blues have been impressive at St Andrew's this season, with Saturday's hosts unbeaten across their opening eight home league battles (W4 D4).

In fact, Birmingham last experienced Second City defeat in the Championship at the beginning of April, and Davies has lost just three home league games since taking charge during the summer of 2024.

Sliding towards the relegation zone, Bolton Wanderers have now won just one of their past seven Championship contests (D2 L4) after losing to West Brom at the Toughsheet Community Stadium earlier in the week.

A second-half penalty from Ruben Rodrigues levelled the scores momentarily following Albion's opener, however, further strikes from Norwegian duo Aune Heggebo and Felix Horn Myhre sentenced the Wanderers to a fourth defeat in their past six games.

Winless in their past five games (D1 L4) at the Toughsheet, Bolton's last three victories have all arrived on the road, with Saturday's underdog visitors beating Norwich City (4-3), Wolverhampton Wanderers (3-1) and Charlton Athletic (1-0) since late September.

There is no doubting that the newly-promoted side are one of the favourites to suffer relegation this season, with Steven Schumacher's troops currently six points clear of the bottom three.

Bolton were defeated on their most recent trip to St Andrew's in October 2024 but were one of only three teams to beat Birmingham during their record-breaking League One title romp of 2024-25.

Birmingham City Championship form:.

Bolton Wanderers Championship form:.

Birmingham defender Ethan Laird missed the Burnley win after picking up a knock at Stoke last weekend, with the right-back a doubt for the Second City match on Saturday.

As a result, Bright Osayi-Samuel is likely to retain his spot in defence, with Dael Fry set to drop out in order to make room for the available-again Christoph Klarer.

Liam Millar, Jhon Solis and Jay Stansfield were rested for the final 15 minutes at Turf Moor, with the trio all set to start once again this weekend.

There is likely to be alteration on the right flank, though, where Patrick Roberts could be the key to unlocking a deep Bolton block.

Bolton rotated leading marksman Sam Dalby out of the starting side on Wednesday but the Englishman is fully expected to return to the XI on Saturday.

Ben Davies could feature against his former loan employers, whilst Samuel Illing-Junior is in line for another start following a bright display against West Brom.

Birmingham City possible starting lineup:.

Beadle; Osayi-Samuel, Neumann, Klarer, Cochrane; Iwata, Solis; Roberts, Stansfield, Millar; Priske.

Bolton Wanderers possible starting lineup:.

Bazunu; Stephenson, Brunt, Forino-Joseph, Conway; Simons, Sheehan; Larrazabal, Ito, Illing-Junior; Dalby.

After winning four straight home matches by an aggregate scoreline of 12-1, Birmingham are the overwhelming favourites for another Second City success this weekend.

Bolton have recent experience of producing a shock result in the West Midlands, however, we feel that Davies's St Andrew's juggernaut will be too strong in this matchup.

City drew 2-2 with Basingstoke Town last Saturday – and the two goals they conceded came when they were playing against ten men.

That was after Kristian Shevchenko – son of one-time Ballon D’or winner Andriy – was sent off in the first half.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Chi coach Darin Killpartrick credited Basingstoke with making it difficult for his team by changing shape when they went down to ten men.

But he noted he was disappointed by the way City defended for the two they let in – and it had to be viewed as an opportunity for three points passed up.

Chi are back at Oaklands Park this Saturday and it’s leaders Uxbridge who are the visitors.

According to recent reports, uxbridge handed City their biggest defeat of the season to date at home in mid-September – it finished 5-0 in Middlesex. And Killpartrick has warned Chi will need to be at their very best to try to get anything out of the game.

Will Sweet and Emmett Dunn were the scorers against Basingstoke as City led 1-0 and 2-1.

Killpartrick said: “It was a missed opportunity for the win against a team who ended with ten men; however when they went down to ten, they changed to a shape that was very difficult to break down.

“We cannot defend – as a team – like we did for their two goals.

Recent findings suggest that “Their first goal upset me the most. Their player has weaved around four or five players and from us that’s not the level we need to produce.

“If you defend like that at this level of football, you will get punished – particularly if you are playing top teams like that.

“But we’ve had a look at it and talked it through with the players and they know we need to defend better than that.”.

One major relief for City is that their long run of Tuesday night matches is over, at least for now.

Killpartrick said the relentless schedule since September had stretched their small squad to the limit and it was great to have a Tuesday when they could concentrate on training, and having a bit of fun as a group too.

Recent findings suggest that another boost is that two key players – midfielder Lloyd Rowlatt and defender Curtis Da Costa – are fit again and pushing for spots. James Sweet has trained again after a hamstring injury.

A massive crowd is hoped for on Saturday, Killpartrick saying: “You’ll see two good teams trying to play entertaining football – we hope for plenty of support.”.

Published: 10:26 EST, 25 November 2026 | Updated: 10:37 EST, 25 November 2026.

James Penrice has warned that Rangers can forget about going top of the table on Saturday if they play like they did for the first 45 minutes against Aberdeen.

Derek McInnes’ side were a goal down at half-time and heading to their first defeat in 14 games after failing to get going against the Dons.

With the manager making three changes at half-time, the Ibrox men scored three times in an incredible 11-minute burst through Ryan Naderi, Djeidi Gassama and Nico Raskin.

And while Aberdeen netted again via Findlay Marshall, Rangers hung on for the win which put them within a point of Celtic.

It has been revealed that ‘It’s a massive incentive for us, but the league isn’t won in November,’ said the defender. ‘Falkirk are playing well. They’ve travelled well away from home too.

James Penrice has warned Rangers they will need to improve if they are to take top spot.

McInnes introduced Tuur Rommens, Findlay Curtis and Kim Min-su at the break with the changes leading to a much-improved display.

Despite chalking up the win which maintained the unbeaten run, Penrice insists the overall show left considerable room for improvement.

It has been revealed that ‘It was very mixed,’ he reflected. ‘We concede in the first half, but then fly out the traps in the second.

Rangers goalscorers Djeidi Gassama, Nico Raskin and Ryan Naderi celebrate against Aberdeen.

‘We could have done that and made it easy for ourselves.’.

Rangers haven’t now tasted defeat since losing away to Czech side Jablonec on August 27. And while not every display in that run has been outstanding, Penrice is encouraged by the fact that the team is showing plenty of character.

Industry observers note that ‘We’ve shown we’ve got a bit of resilience,’ he mentioned. ‘It’s not a bad trait to be winning games and scoring late on. We’re doing that. But as players we want to make the game as easy as possible.

The South Korean, an £8.5million summer signing from Girona, has yet to find the net in 14 appearances with his sole assist coming against Motherwell last Saturday.

It has been revealed that ‘You can see he wants it so bad. He probably just needs to calm down in front of goal.

It has been revealed that ‘I thought that was the one when he chopped inside. I thought he was scoring, but he put it into row Z.

Kim Min-su has impressed for Rangers but is still waiting to score his first goal for the club.

‘It wasn’t ideal, but he was still happy afterward because we won the game.

Recent findings suggest that ‘You can see in his game that, at every opportunity, he’s trying to get a shot away. It will come and hopefully it comes at a perfect time.

It has been revealed that ‘There’s a reason these players are at Ibrox — it’s because they’re extremely talented. It’s just that last bit but they’re very young.

According to recent reports, ‘Min-su’s game isn’t just goals and assists. He’s a really talented footballer who creates problems for teams. He’s been a massive part of why we’re on this run. You can all see it.

‘It’s about more than goals and assists, but if he adds that to his game, he’s only going to go on and have a very successful career.

Two of those goals came off the bench against Besiktas last time out in the Europa League when he helped inspire a comeback victory.

It has been revealed that “Obviously, on Portuguese soil, he’ll want to do well. But remember, he’s been out of the game for about 18, 19, 20 months. It’s a long, long time to try and get that sort of max fitness again, but he’s improving each game.”.

Forrest drew level with Scott Brown’s Celtic record of 127 European appearances.
